definition: An architecture that reuses one shared stack of layers across several recursion steps while lightweight routers assign each token its own recursion depth, so easy tokens exit early and hard tokens think for longer.
details: MoR combines two efficiency levers at once: parameter sharing, by looping the same block instead of building a deeper stack, and adaptive computation, by letting a router decide how many passes each token receives. Because only tokens still active at a given depth attend to one another, quadratic attention is confined to that subset and only their key-value pairs need caching; a KV-sharing variant reuses the first recursion's pairs to cut memory further. Across 135M–1.7B parameter models MoR lowers validation perplexity and raises throughput at equal training FLOPs, forming a new Pareto frontier against vanilla and earlier recursive baselines.

citation.title: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
